positive: AsyncLocalStorage-based RLS context — request-scoped identity passed through AsyncLocalStorage (not process globals). Found in src/middleware/rls.ts:45-49.
Transaction-scoped GUC for PgBouncer safety — Production RLS uses TRANSACTION-scoped set_app_user_id() inside transactions, not SESSION-scoped. Found in src/middleware/rls.ts:236-278.

Ownership Guard pattern — Centralized ownership checks in src/services/ownership/ownership.guard.ts with explicit methods for each resource type (application, timeline, company, recruiter, extractionRun, fact, provenance, canonicalIntelligence).
userOwnershipFilter() dual-matching — Handles legacy-to-UUID migration by matching both userId (FK) and legacyUserId (string) in OR clauses. Found in src/utils/user-ownership.ts:14-25.

Idempotency service for email processing — 2-phase claim/commit pattern prevents duplicate application creation from email processing. Found in src/services/application-command/application-command.service.ts:141-397.

Layered placement caching — In-process TTL (1 min) -> Redis (5 min) -> DB. Deterministic shard key computation avoids DB reads for shard resolution. Found in src/services/placement/placement.service.ts:154-360.

Role-segregated database connections — config/index.ts validates production credentials with least-privilege roles (app_runtime, app_worker, app_migration, app_readonly, app_admin). src/config/database.ts:93-104.
Dual-Redis architecture — Separate RedisQueue (BullMQ/job state) and RedisCache (cache/rate-limiting/OAuth state). Found in src/config/index.ts:62-98.
Content-addressed resume storage — SHA-256 hash deduplication with quarantine->clean bucket promotion. Found in src/services/resume/resume-upload.service.ts:109-289.
Durable checkpoint service — Atomic checkpoint advancement with optimistic locking for Gmail sync resumability. Found in src/services/gmail/ingestion/gmail-ingestion.service.ts.

Singleton pattern with dependency injection support — Services accept dependencies via constructor for testability while exporting singletons for production use (e.g., cellService, opportunityService).
negative: Global Prisma client stash — globalThis.prisma and globalThis.prismaReplica used for hot-reload safety in dev, persist in production. src/config/database.ts:47-50, 134-138, 146-161.

Legacy dual-ID field pollution — Every user-scoped table has both userId (UUID FK) and legacyUserId (string). Doubles ownership check surface area and creates divergence risk during migration transitions.
Company is global, not user-scoped — Company records are global/shared across users. Ownership derived via application relationships. src/services/company/company.service.ts:190-233.

Opportunity is global, not user-scoped — Opportunities live in a global table keyed by (company, title, location). Multiple users applying to the same role share the same opportunity record. src/services/opportunity/opportunity.service.ts:1-27.

RLS middleware is a no-op in production — The Prisma interceptor in attachRlsMiddleware uses SESSION-scoped GUC which is discarded under PgBouncer transaction pooling. Production relies on callers remembering to wrap in withRlsTransaction(). src/middleware/rls.ts:184-220.

In-process placement cache is process-global state — PlacementService maintains a Map<string, InProcessEntry> (up to 4096 entries) not shared across processes. src/services/placement/placement.service.ts:154-157, 287-308.
Feature flag stuck at false — features.asyncEmailProcessing hardcoded false, rendering async email processing path dead code in production. src/config/features.ts:1-3.

JobApplication.findMany() without user filter at merge layer — ApplicationMergeService.findMatch loads all applications for user without application-level ownership pre-filter. Relies on caller passing correct userId. src/services/application-merge/application-merge.service.ts:33-35.

TokenService singleton instantiated at module load — tokenService created as singleton at module top-level. If config.jwtSecret missing, module fails to load. src/services/auth/token.service.ts:199-200.

Bulk in-memory merge scanning — Application merge loads all applications for user into memory for confidence scoring. Bounded per-user but won't scale indefinitely. src/services/application-merge/application-merge.service.ts:30-33.

process_env_direct_usage_in_business_log.description: Found 14 instances of process.env usage directly in business logic (not through config). Most are in test files, but src/utils/encryption.ts and src/infrastructure/crypto/crypto-service.ts reference process.env.ACTIVE_ENCRYPTION_KEY_VERSION and process.env.CRYPTO_BACKEND directly.
process_env_direct_usage_in_business_log.recommendation: All env var access should route through src/config/index.ts to ensure consistent validation and allow mocking.

any_type_usage_in_production_code.recommendation: Replace any with proper Prisma.JsonValue or domain types.

rls_middleware_noop_in_production.description: The attachRlsMiddleware Prisma interceptor uses set_app_user_id_session() which is SESSION-scoped and gets reset under PgBouncer transaction pooling. In production this becomes a no-op unless callers explicitly wrap in withRlsTransaction(). Each service method must be audited to ensure every user-scoped query uses withRlsTransaction or withRequestContextTransaction.
services_using_raw_prisma_without_rls_wr: src/services/gmail/ingestion/gmail-ingestion.service.ts:372-401 (processAndSaveBatch upsert uses raw prisma, no RLS)
rls_middleware_noop_in_production.recommendation: Either enforce mandatory RLS transaction wrapping via a custom $extends wrapper, or add fail-closed logging in attachRlsMiddleware for production that breaks requests when SESSION GUC fails.

instances.query: SELECT set_app_user_id_session($1) — session-scoped, no-op under PgBouncer

direct_raw_sql_execution.recommendation: All raw SQL is currently limited to RLS GUC setting which is acceptable. No other raw SQL patterns found.

test_environment_auth_bypass.description: requireAuth middleware accepts x-user-id header bypassing JWT verification when NODE_ENV=test. Guarded by environment check. src/middleware/auth.ts:59-67.
test_environment_auth_bypass.recommendation: Ensure NODE_ENV=test is never deployed to production. Add CI gate that fails if NODE_ENV=test references appear in Dockerfile or deployment configs.

race_condition_mitigation_present.description: User creation handles P2002 unique constraint violations by retrying findUnique. src/services/user/user.service.ts:94-99. Resume upload handles hash collision race condition. src/services/resume/resume-upload.service.ts:153-169.
race_condition_mitigation_present.recommendation: Continue pattern. Consider adding database-level retry helpers for other upsert paths.

denormalized_fields.description: JobApplication denormalizes companyName and companyDomain even though it has companyId FK. If Company.name changes, existing JobApplication rows retain stale denormalized data. application-command.service.ts:268-269 updates these on merge but not on initial create from companyService.resolveCompany which may return canonical name different from input.
Role data is denormalized from Opportunity. If Opportunity.title changes, JobApplication retains old value. May be intentional snapshot semantics but should be documented.
Same pattern - opportunity-level fields denormalized to application level. Opportunity changes do not propagate.

placementService reads user.region and user.shardKey from DB. Set at creation time. If user updates region via setUserRegion, DB values update atomically. The in-process cache for these has 1-minute TTL which could serve stale values during region change.

missing_unique_constraints.description: Opportunity resolution uses fuzzy text matching (normalizeTitle, titlesAreSimilar, normalizeLocation) rather than DB unique constraints. The Opportunity table has @@index([companyId]) and @@index([title]) but no composite unique constraint on (companyId, title, location). Concurrent resolution of the same opportunity can create duplicates before the mutex acquires. The application-level mutex (line 156 of opportunity.service.ts) mitigates this but is not a database guarantee.
missing_unique_constraints.recommendation: Add a normalized_title + normalized_location computed column with unique index on (companyId, normalized_title, normalized_location) to prevent duplicates at the DB level.

missing_unique_constraints.description: Schema has @@unique([legacyUserId, providerMessageId], name: unique_user_message). Used correctly in gmail-ingestion.service.ts for deduplication.
Schema has @@unique([legacyUserId, provider, emailAddress], name: unique_user_provider_email).
Schema has @@unique on key. Used for idempotency gate.

redis_only_business_state.state: Refresh tokens stored in Redis with 7-day TTL
redis_only_business_state.description: All refresh tokens are Redis-only. If Redis loses data (flush, restart without persistence), ALL users are simultaneously logged out.
redis_only_business_state.recommendation: Consider storing refresh tokens in DB with Redis as cache layer for revocation checks.

redis_only_business_state.state: CSRF state tokens stored in Redis
redis_only_business_state.description: OAuth flow state stored ephemerally in Redis. Short TTL, low blast radius if lost.
If Redis loses idempotency records between claim and commit, duplicate processing can occur. The 60-day TTL in DB provides backstop.
redis_only_business_state.recommendation: Consider dual-write idempotency claims to DB on claim, with Redis as cache.

redis_only_business_state.description: Non-durable, process-local state. In multi-worker deployments, workers may serve stale placement for up to 1 minute after region change.

cross_user_access_patterns.description: Company records are user-shared. Ownership checked via application-company relationship. Company details can change and affect all users.
Opportunity records resolve across users. Enriching an opportunity benefits all users pointing to it.
cross_user_access_patterns.recommendation: Ensure opportunity mutations are idempotent and non-destructive (only enrich, never replace).

cross_user_access_patterns.description: ApplicationMergeService only processes applications for the current user (filtered by userOwnershipFilter). No cross-user merge possible.

non_idempotent_operations.description: Each observation call creates a new OpportunityObservation and supersedes ALL previous current observations. If called twice with same input, two new observations are created. Idempotent in effect (only one current) but creates duplicate rows.
non_idempotent_operations.mitigation: Idempotency keyed by sourceEmailId via application-command.service.ts preflight check.

non_idempotent_operations.description: Uses 2-phase claim/commit idempotency pattern. Produces exactly one application per email.
SHA-256 content hash with P2002 race condition handling. Multiple identical uploads produce one resumeHash and one userResume.

missing_ownership_checks.description: getApplicationResume queries ApplicationResume by applicationId without verifying the requesting user owns the application. Any authenticated user who knows an applicationId can read associated resume metadata.
missing_ownership_checks.recommendation: Add ownershipGuard.ensureApplicationAccess(userId, applicationId) or userOwnershipFilter on the query.

missing_ownership_checks.check: No userId parameter; ownership not verified
missing_ownership_checks.description: linkApplicationResume does not accept a userId parameter and does not verify ownership of the application or resume. Called from application-command.service.ts with transaction context, so ownership assumed from caller.
missing_ownership_checks.recommendation: Add userId parameter and verify ownership of both application and active resume row within the transaction.

missing_ownership_checks.check: No userId verification; connectionId trusted alone
missing_ownership_checks.description: refreshAccessToken and getValidAccessToken accept connectionId without verifying requesting user owns that connection. TokenService.rotateTokenPair also accepts userId without verifying it matches refresh token.
missing_ownership_checks.recommendation: Verify userId owns the connectionId when called from user-facing endpoints.

full_table_scans.description: Loads ALL applications for a user into memory for confidence scoring. Bounded per-user but unbounded system-wide if users have large application sets.
full_table_scans.recommendation: Add companyId filter or paginate candidates. For users with 1000+ applications, this becomes expensive.

full_table_scans.description: Joins through applications to filter by user ownership. For users with thousands of applications across many companies, could produce large intermediate result sets.
Pre-filters candidates by companyId + title contains, bounded by company opportunity count. Mutex prevents concurrency storms.

in_memory_merge_loops.algorithm: O(n*m) confidence scoring across all user applications
in_memory_merge_loops.description: For each incoming email, iterates all user applications computing text similarity. Linear scaling with application count.

bounded_batch_processing.description: Initial sync capped at 1000 messages to prevent runaway processing. Incremental syncs bounded by Gmail API history pages.

placement_cache_sizing.description: In multi-worker deployments, each worker maintains its own cache. User hitting different workers may experience cache misses.

cell_awareness.cell_routing_integration: CellRoutingService.resolveUserRouting combines placementService + cellService. CellService.getDeterministicCellId uses computeShardKey + region to build cellId. src/services/cell/cell.service.ts:29-32.
cell_awareness.rls_cell_id_source: RLS context gets cellId from req (set by placement middleware), NOT from AsyncLocalStorage RLS context directly. src/middleware/rls.ts:96. This means cellId is request-header-derived, not computed server-side from placementService.
cell_awareness.risk: MEDIUM — If placement middleware computes a cellId that differs from placementService's authoritative resolution (due to cache stale or hint mismatch), the cellId in RLS context could diverge from the actual home cell.

ownership_check_consistency.inconsistency: Some guards use OR filters (userOwnershipFilter) which match both userId AND legacyUserId. Others use direct userId comparison. During the legacy migration window, a user could have rows where userId is set but legacyUserId is different, or vice versa.
ownership_check_consistency.recommendation: Standardize all guards to use userOwnershipFilter() for consistency.

GmailOAuthService accepts connectionId without userId ownership verification
Opportunity resolution lacks DB-level unique constraint for fuzzy matches

Bulk in-memory merge scanning for large application sets

conclusion.summary: The codebase demonstrates sophisticated architectural patterns including AsyncLocalStorage-based RLS context management, transaction-scoped GUC for PgBouncer safety, idempotency services, layered caching, and a comprehensive ownership guard system. Primary concerns are: (1) RLS is not enforced at the database interceptor layer in production — each service must remember to wrap in transactions, (2) several endpoints bypass ownership checks (notably getApplicationResume), (3) process-global state exists for Prisma clients and placement caching, and (4) shadow duplicate IDs (legacyUserId + userId) create ongoing audit complexity. These are mitigable concerns rather than fundamental architectural failures.
priority_recommendations: Wrap ALL user-scoped Prisma queries in withRlsTransaction() or withRequestContextTransaction() — or use a Prisma $extends wrapper that enforces this automatically.
Add ownership check to ResumeUploadService.getApplicationResume() — currently allows reading any application resume by ID without verifying ownership.
Add unique index on Opportunity (companyId, normalized_title, normalized_location) to prevent fuzzy-match duplicates at DB level.
Audit all globalThis stashes for production persistence concerns.
Migrate refresh tokens from Redis-only to DB-durable storage with Redis cache layer.
